title: International Excellence and Impact Awards
subtitle: Celebrating Excellence in Research, Education, Industry, Entrepreneurship and Responsible Innovation
intro: The Organizing Committee of the International Conference on Trustworthy AI and Intelligent IoT Systems (TAIIS 2026) invites nominations for the TAIIS 2026 International Excellence and Impact Awards.

The awards recognise researchers, academicians, educators, industry professionals, innovators, entrepreneurs, start-ups, research teams, and institutions that have made meaningful and verifiable contributions to artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, intelligent IoT systems, computing, education, entrepreneurship, and responsible technological development.
The awards will be presented during TAIIS 2026, to be held from December 3–5, 2026, at Asia University, Taichung, Taiwan.
importantDatesNote: The Awards Committee reserves the right to revise the schedule where necessary. Any changes will be announced on this page.

awardCategoriesNote: Not every category must necessarily result in an award. The Awards Committee may withhold or combine a category when the nominations do not meet the expected standards or when an insufficient number of eligible nominations is received.
whoCanBeNominatedNote: Nominations are open internationally. The nominee’s contribution should be relevant to research, education, technology, innovation, entrepreneurship, or societal development.
whoCanSubmitIntro: A nomination may be submitted through:
whoCanSubmit: Nomination by an academic or professional peer
Nomination by a university, department, or research centre
Nomination by an employer or industry organisation
Recommendation by a TAIIS committee member or invited expert
whoCanSubmitNote: A third-party nominator must obtain the nominee’s consent before submitting personal information or supporting documentation.
nominationRequirements: Nominee summary — provide a brief summary of why this nominee deserves the recognition
Key achievement — list the most significant achievements and contributions
Impact description — describe the nominee’s impact on education, industry, and society
Innovation and uniqueness — describe what makes the nominee’s approach innovative and unique

Supporting documents (Google Drive link) — upload all supporting documents (CV, letters of recommendation, testimonials, research documents, award certificates, impact reports, media coverage, and related materials) to a single Google Drive folder and provide the folder link in the nomination form. Set sharing permission to “Anyone with the link can view” so documents can be accessed without a permission request.
nominationRequirementsNote: All fields on the online nomination form are required. General promotional statements without verifiable supporting documents may not be considered sufficient.
youngResearchersParagraphs: Candidates for the Best Young Researcher Award should normally be within ten years of receiving their highest research degree as of the nomination deadline.

Documented career interruptions—including parental leave, long-term illness, caregiving responsibilities, compulsory national service, or other exceptional circumstances—may be considered when determining eligibility.
The evaluation will focus on research independence, originality, quality, demonstrated impact, and future potential rather than age alone.

howToSubmitSteps.title: Step 1: Select the Appropriate Category
howToSubmitSteps.description: Review all award categories and choose the award name that best represents the nominee’s principal contribution.

howToSubmitSteps.title: Step 2: Prepare Supporting Documents
howToSubmitSteps.description: Prepare the nominee summary, key achievements, impact description, and innovation statement. Upload CV, letters of recommendation, testimonials, research documents, certificates, impact reports, media coverage, and other supporting materials to one Google Drive folder with link sharing set to “Anyone with the link can view.”

howToSubmitSteps.title: Step 3: Complete the Online Form
howToSubmitSteps.description: Submit all required information through the official online nomination form, including the Google Drive folder link.

howToSubmitSteps.title: Step 4: Receive Confirmation
howToSubmitSteps.description: After successful submission, the nominator will receive an acknowledgement. The Awards Committee may request additional information or clarification during evaluation.

nominationFormNote: Nominations sent through informal social-media messages will not be considered.

evaluationProcess.title: Stage 1: Eligibility and Completeness Check
evaluationProcess.description: The Awards committee will verify the selected category, eligibility of the nominee, completeness of the submission, and availability of supporting evidence.

evaluationProcess.title: Stage 2: Conflict-of-Interest Review
evaluationProcess.description: Nominations will be assigned to evaluators who do not have a direct supervisory, institutional, financial, or personal conflict with the nominee.

evaluationProcess.title: Stage 3: Independent Expert Evaluation
evaluationProcess.description: Each eligible nomination will normally be assessed independently by at least two experts using the published evaluation framework.

evaluationProcess.title: Stage 4: Evidence Verification
evaluationProcess.description: The committee may verify publications, patents, affiliations, start-up registrations, products, deployments, partnerships, and other important claims. Additional clarification may be requested.

evaluationProcess.title: Stage 5: Committee Deliberation
evaluationProcess.description: Shortlisted nominations will be considered by the Awards Committee, taking into account the expert evaluations and category-specific requirements.

evaluationProcess.title: Stage 6: Final Approval
evaluationProcess.description: The final recommendations will be reviewed and approved by the authorised TAIIS 2026 Awards Committee.

evaluationCriteria.criterion: Verifiable academic, industrial, economic, or societal impact

evaluationCriteriaNotes: The committee may adjust the emphasis according to the category. For example:
Academic awards will emphasise research, education, mentorship, and scholarly leadership;
Industry awards will emphasise implementation, adoption, reliability, and measurable value;
Start-up awards will emphasise innovation, market validation, scalability, governance, and growth potential;
Global awards will emphasise international reach, cross-border collaboration, inclusiveness, and societal impact;
Institutional awards will emphasise strategy, continuity, ecosystem development, and verified organisational outcomes.
integrityItems: Nomination and evaluation will be based on merit and verifiable evidence.
Submission of a nomination does not guarantee selection.
Evaluators must disclose relevant conflicts of interest.
False, misleading, plagiarised, or fabricated information may result in disqualification.
The committee may contact the nominee’s institution or nominated referees to verify important claims.
Confidential nomination material will be used only for evaluation and administrative purposes.
Information about selected recipients will be published only after confirmation and consent.
Normally, an individual or organisation will receive no more than one nomination-based award in the same edition.
The Awards Committee may withhold an award when no nomination meets the required standard.
Decisions of the Awards Committee will be final.
recognitionItems: Recognition during the TAIIS 2026 Award Ceremony
An award citation published on the conference website
Recognition through official conference communication and social-media channels
Inclusion in the TAIIS 2026 list of award recipients

faq.question: Is self-nomination permitted?
faq.answer: Yes. Self-nomination, peer nomination, and institutional nomination are permitted.

faq.question: Is submitting a conference paper compulsory?
faq.answer: No. These nomination-based awards are independent of conference paper submission and publication.

faq.question: Can one person be nominated for multiple categories?
faq.answer: A nominee may be proposed for a maximum of two categories. However, the committee will normally confer only one nomination-based award on the same recipient.

faq.question: Will every announced category have a winner?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. An award will be presented only when at least one nomination meets the required quality standard.

faq.question: Is physical attendance compulsory?
faq.answer: Physical participation is encouraged but is not a condition of selection. Online recognition may be approved for recipients unable to travel.

faq.question: Will nomination materials be published?
faq.answer: Nomination documents will not be publicly released. For selected recipients, only the approved biography, photograph, award citation, and relevant public links may be published.

faq.question: Are awards connected with Springer publication?
faq.answer: No. These awards are independently administered by the TAIIS 2026 Organizing Committee. They have no influence on Springer Nature’s editorial, quality-control, or publication decisions.
